title: Cairn module manifest (YAML)
$comment: A module is interpretation: it says what a reading MEANS, across the dongle, server, web and app at once. The core is GPS logging management -- capture, custody, receipt-gated prune, decode, trips -- and a module never touches it. DRAFT: the identifier keeps its -draft suffix until the gate in README.md is met. JSON Schema states structure only; what it cannot state is in spec.md and is enforced by the checker: id equals the directory name, exactly one module owns each derived column, derivation order has no cycle, a metric's source view is declared by the module, a query's parameters all appear in its SQL, and a stub claims nothing. NOTE ON WHAT IS ABSENT: there is deliberately no field here through which a module could ask for bundle bytes, a key, a receipt, a prune decision or a network listener. That is structural, not a convention -- additionalProperties is false throughout, so such a request cannot be spelled.

id.$comment: Equals the module's directory name. Namespaces its derived columns, views, queries and generated symbols.

status.$comment: The same three words, with the same meanings, as engine/v1. stub: identity only, claims nothing -- a module may legitimately be nothing but a manifest. derived: extracted from code that already worked. verified: checked against the real car.

store.$comment: Columns this module reads, as table.column. Checked against store/v1's schema.json, so a typo fails validation rather than a page. May name a column another module derives; the loader then orders the derivations, and a cycle is an error.

engine_fields.$comment: Capture-record fields the dongle must be recording, from engine/v1's acquisition `field` enum. A module STATES a requirement; it cannot make a dongle poll a PID the engine profile does not declare. Unmet at build time is a build error.

type.$comment: A DuckDB type, from store/v1's vocabulary.

expr.$comment: A SQL scalar expression over the columns of the row's own table, evaluated by DuckDB during load. SQL, not a new little language: the host already has an evaluator, and adding one would be the thing the retired plugin system got wrong.

derives.$comment: Columns this module defines on core tables. Exactly one module may own a column. When the owning module is absent the column exists and is all-null, which is what the store already says about a car that never reported the input.

metrics.$comment: What this module contributes to the generic machinery: v_metric_samples, v_health_stats, v_tune_effect, the trip-insight list and the dashboard highlights. Replaces the literal metric list those views carry today.

views.$comment: SQL files creating this module's views, applied in order. Every view must be named v_<module id>_* or be listed in store/v1 under a grandfathered name.

queries.$comment: The module's named, parameterised queries (queries.schema.json). Named queries are how raw SQL leaves the web repository: a route calls a query by name with typed parameters, and no string is ever spliced into SQL.

group.$comment: detail entries are hidden until the reader asks for them, or is on one.

vehicle_scope.$comment: single means this page always answers for exactly one car. A trim map or boost curve pooled over an N20 and a B58 describes no real engine, so it is not a default to get wrong.

ios.$comment: The app's participation is deliberately narrow. Live gauges come from metrics[].ios_gauge, and the app's richer analysis arrives over sync/v1 as the insight payload the server already produces, so a new module usually needs no iOS change at all. The phone is the uplink and a reader, not a sixth place to reimplement a trim map.

rel_path.$comment: A path inside the module's own directory. No leading slash and no `..`: a module cannot reach outside itself.

engine_field.$comment: MUST stay identical to the `field` enum in engine/v1's acquisition.schema.json. The checker compares the two, so they cannot drift.

key.$comment: Also an engine/v1 analysis `signals[].key`, which is how a reading finds its limits. A metric with no matching signal is shown without a verdict -- never called normal.

unit.$comment: Empty for a dimensionless metric such as lambda.

sample.$comment: What one observation is. A CLOSED enum on purpose: it decides how v_metric_samples counts, and `enough observations to judge` means nothing if a module can invent its own unit. boost is per-pull and the trims are per-boot, so two is already the minimum.

trip_insight.$comment: Contributed to the trip-detail insight list. Without a contribution point like this, moving a module's code out of the core fails at the shell pages that pull module-owned metrics.

field.$comment: A decoded property name on the app's live-telemetry record.
